title: Kobbie Mainoo to sign new Manchester United contract
content:
Kobbie Mainoo is signing a new contract at Manchester United.

The Athletic reported on March 20 that United were close to an agreement with the midfielder over a new contract, with negotiations at an advanced stage for a deal to 2031 on an improved salary.

Mainoo’s new terms, which he will officially sign on Wednesday, will now put him among the club’s first-team-level earners.

The 21-year-old was recalled to Thomas Tuchel’s England squad last month, the German head coach’s final one before the provisional World Cup squad is named. He played 21 minutes as a substitute in the 1-1 draw against Uruguay and started against Japan four days later, playing 71 minutes.

Mainoo had requested a loan move away after falling out of favour under former United head coach Ruben Amorim. The club did not sanction a departure, however, and after the Portuguese’s sacking in January he regained his place in the starting line-up.

Under Michael Carrick, the England international has impressed, starting 12 of the club’s 13 league games — missing the home defeat to Leeds United on April 13 through injury.

Mainoo, one of the most promising players to come from United’s academy in recent years, made his first-team debut for the club in January 2023.

He quickly established himself in the side’s starting XI under Erik ten Hag, made his senior debut for England in March 2024, and went on to play a starring role for his country during the 2024 European Championship.

The Portuguese coach’s decision to leave out the midfielder was routinely questioned by fans. Pictures emerged on social media during United’s 4-4 draw with Bournemouth at Old Trafford in December, showing Mainoo’s brother wearing a t-shirt with the text “Free Kobbie Mainoo”.

Mainoo has made 98 senior appearances for United, 26 of which have come this term despite picking up a calf injury in December.

As soon as Ruben Amorim was sacked, securing Mainoo’s future was high on the agenda at United. He has been on the same contract since February 2023 and while that deal included pay rises he has been earning far less than his status, at around £25,000 per week.

Being out of the team under Amorim meant Mainoo had no desire to sign fresh terms at United but he has become a mainstay of Michael Carrick’s side. United have long wanted to extend his contract beyond 2027, entering initial talks last year, and negotiations have progressed since January.

United’s contracts are now more incentivised, which has been a feature of discussions over Mainoo’s contact. Finding an agreement is a major boost for the club.
